scenes.title: Tuning and pitch
scenes.blurb: Hold the note, a little high, a little low, in tune.

kn.rule: Tens plus units: drop the tu, join the unit. ippattu + ondu = ippattondu; before mooru and naalku drop the whole ttu: ippatmooru.

ta.rule: Tens change their tail to tthi and the unit follows: irubatthi onnu. Ninety is thonnootri.

hi.rule: Every number from 21 to 99 is its own word. Hear the family: the unit sits in FRONT (ik, ba, tir, chau, pach, chhi, sat, ath) and nine is un plus the next ten.

ml.rule: Malayalam joins the ten to the unit: irupathi onnu is twenty one, muppathi anchu is thirty five. The ten loses its last sound and the unit follows.

soundNote.kn: A doubled vowel is held about twice as long. Hold aa, ee, oo like a long note; a, i, u are short notes. Stretching the last vowel to aa also turns any sentence into a question.
soundNote.hi: A doubled vowel is held longer: kal versus kaal. Hindi also has a soft breath after some consonants (bh, dh, kh): bhaai, not baai.
soundNote.ta: A doubled vowel is held longer: pal versus paal. zh (as in Tamizh, vaazhai) is a soft rolled sound between l and r; most learners start with l and are understood.
soundNote.ml: Malayalam hears a long vowel as a different word, and it hears double consonants too: kali and kaali, ari and aari. Hold the long one for two beats and the single consonant light.
